classification.difficultyReason: Convert paired results into a scatterplot, choose a reasonable best-fit line, read forward and reverse predictions, and distinguish extrapolation using the relevant observed range.

inlines.text: The results of a group of students on Mathematics and Science tests are compared.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show these results as a scatterplot.

spec.description: Blank square grid at 5-mark intervals, displayed ranges 55–105 horizontally and 50–95 vertically, broken axes, arrowheads and supplied title.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal variable M; vertical variable S. No supplied points or line.
spec.answerVisibility: The grid and labels remain visible; plotted points are solution-only.

answer.short: Plot the ten points shown in the solution scatterplot.
answer.worked: Use Mathematics marks on the horizontal axis and Science marks on the vertical axis. Plot $(64,68)$, $(67,73)$, $(69,68)$, $(70,75)$, $(73,78)$, $(74,73)$, $(77,77)$, $(82,84)$, $(84,86)$ and $(85,89)$.

spec.description: Completed scatterplot with all ten paired marks, preserving the supplied grid, scales, broken axes and title.
spec.mathematics: Points are the exact paired values from the native table.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Describe the strength of the relationship as strong, moderate, or weak.

answer.worked: Strong: the points lie close to an upward-sloping straight line.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use a line of best fit to estimate the score in Science of a student who scores 80 in Mathematics.

answer.short: Approximately 82 marks; estimates depend on the line drawn.
answer.worked: Draw a straight line through the centre of the points, with roughly equal numbers on each side. From 80 on the Mathematics axis, move vertically to the line, then horizontally to the Science axis: approximately 82 marks. Other reasonable by-eye lines give slightly different estimates.

spec.description: An acceptable example best-fit line and graphical reading guides; the equation is an authoring construction and is not printed.
spec.mathematics: Example line S=8+0.93M gives S=82.4 at M=80 and M=52/0.93 at S=60; graphical estimates round to 82 and 56 marks.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Use the line of best fit to estimate the score in Mathematics of a student who scores 60 in Science.

answer.short: Approximately 56 marks; estimates depend on the line drawn.
answer.worked: Extend the same line of best fit towards the lower marks. From 60 on the Science axis, move horizontally to the extended line, then vertically to the Mathematics axis: approximately 56 marks. Other reasonable by-eye lines give slightly different estimates.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Is part c or part d an example of extrapolation?

answer.short: Part d, because 60 in Science is outside the observed range.
answer.worked: Part d is extrapolation: the observed Science marks range from 68 to 89, so 60 lies outside the existing data. Part c is interpolation because 80 lies within the observed Mathematics range of 64 to 85.
